questionText: What is the range of the dataset {15, 20, 25, 30, 35}?
calculationDraft: Correct: The range of a dataset is the difference between the largest and smallest values. For the dataset {15, 20, 25, 30, 35}, the largest value is 35 and the smallest value is 15. Range = largest - smallest = 35 - 15 = 20. Distractor A (Computational Error): Student subtracts smallest from largest but forgets to include the endpoints, Range = 35 - 20 = 15. Distractor B (Conceptual Misconception): Student calculates the mean instead of the range, Range = (15 + 20 + 25 + 30 + 35) / 5 = 25. Distractor C (Trap): Student finds the median and mistakes it for the range, Median = 25, Range = 25.

alternateQuestions.questionText: What is the interquartile range (IQR) of the dataset {12, 15, 18, 20, 22, 25, 30}?
alternateQuestions.calculationDraft: Correct: The interquartile range (IQR) of a dataset is the difference between the third quartile (Q3) and the first quartile (Q1). For the dataset {12, 15, 18, 20, 22, 25, 30}, Q3 = 25 and Q1 = 15. IQR = Q3 - Q1 = 25 - 15 = 10. Distractor A (Computational Error): Student adds Q3 and Q1 instead of subtracting, IQR = 25 + 15 = 40. Distractor B (Conceptual Misconception): Student calculates the range instead of the IQR, Range = 30 - 12 = 18. Distractor C (Trap): Student finds the median and mistakes it for the IQR, Median = 20, IQR = 20.

relatedContent.conceptSummary: Measures of dispersion describe the spread of a dataset. The range is the difference between the largest and smallest values, while the interquartile range (IQR) is the difference between the third and first quartiles.
